Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verse 1:

(p-490) Surat "At-Taghabun" (The Mutual Loss and Gain)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah. His is the dominion, and His is the praise, and He is over all things Competent.﴾ The two adverbial phrases (al-zarfan) have been placed first so that their placement indicates the exclusivity of dominion (al-mulk) and praise (al-hamd) to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is because dominion in the true sense belongs to Him, since He is the originator of everything and the one who sustains it. Likewise praise, because the roots and branches of blessings all come from Him. As for the dominion of others, it is a delegation from Him and a trust entrusted (istir'a') to them. And praising others is only a reckoning that Allah's blessing has flowed through their hand.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verse 2:

﴿He it is who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾. That is: among you is one who comes to disbelief and performs it, and among you is one who comes to faith and performs it. What indicates this is His saying: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, that is, Knowing and Seeing of your disbelief and your faith, which are among your deeds. The meaning is: "He it is who bestowed upon you graciously the foundation of all blessings, which is creation and bringing into existence from non-existence. It was incumbent upon you all to be grateful. So what is wrong with you that you have divided into groups, some of you disbelievers and some of you believers?!" He mentioned disbelief first because it is the dominant and most prevalent among them. This is also a refutation of the one who says "the intermediate position between the two positions" (al-manzila bayn al-manzilatayn, the doctrine of an intermediate status between belief and disbelief). It has also been said: "He it is who created you, so among you is one who disbelieves in the creation, and they are the Dahriyya (the materialists who deny a Creator and attribute events to time), and among you is one who believes in it."

(p-491) ﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾, with consummate wisdom, which is that He made them the abode of the responsible beings (mukallafun), so that they might act and He might then recompense them.

﴿And He shaped you and perfected your shapes﴾, i.e., He made you the most beautiful of all animals and the most splendid of them. The evidence for this is that a human being does not wish that his form were other than what he sees of the other forms. And among the beauty of his form is that he was created upright, not hunched over. As for one who is ugly, deformed in form and repulsive in make-up, there is no repulsiveness in that (i.e., in the human form as such); rather, beauty has degrees, and because it falls short of what is above it, it is not considered pleasing, yet it does not fall outside the bounds of beauty. The sages said: "Two things have no limit: beauty and eloquence."

﴿And to Him is the final return﴾, so make your inner selves beautiful, just as He made your forms beautiful.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verse 4:

﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose, and Allah is All-Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ He alerted, by His knowledge, to what is in the heavens and the earth; then by His knowledge of what the servants conceal and disclose; then by His knowledge of what is within the breasts, that nothing of the universals (al-kulliyyat) and the particulars (al-juz'iyyat) is hidden from Him. Therefore His due is that He be feared and beware of, and that one not dare to do anything that contradicts His pleasure. The repetition of knowledge carries the sense of the repetition of warning (al-wa'id). And everything He mentioned after His saying: ﴿So among you is a disbeliever, and among you is a believer﴾ [al-Taghabun: 2], carries the sense of a warning against disbelief, and a denunciation that the Creator should be disobeyed, and that His blessing should not be thanked.

﴿Has there not come to you﴾: the address is to the disbelievers of Makkah,

﴿the news of those who disbelieved before you﴾, meaning the people of Noah, Hud, Salih, and Lot,

﴿so they tasted the evil consequence of their affair﴾, i.e., they tasted the evil consequence of their disbelief in this world (al-dunya),

﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾, in the hereafter (al-'uqba).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verse 6:

﴿That﴾, a reference to what was mentioned of the retribution (wabal) they tasted in this world, and what has been prepared for them of punishment in the Hereafter.

﴿Because﴾, because the matter (al-sha'n) and the account (al-hadith) [is that]:

﴿their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs﴾, with miracles (mu'jizat).

﴿So they said: "Shall mere humans guide us?"﴾ They denied that messengership could be for humans, yet they did not deny the worship of a stone.

﴿So they disbelieved﴾, in the messengers.

﴿And turned away﴾, from faith.

﴿And Allah was free of need﴾, the expression is unrestricted so that it encompasses everything, and among its scope is their faith and their obedience.

﴿And Allah is Self-Sufficient﴾, free of need from His creation,

﴿Praiseworthy﴾, in His doing.

(p-٤٩٢)﴿Those who disbelieved claim﴾, i.e., the people of Mecca. *Al-za'm* (asserting, claiming knowledge) is the claim to knowledge, and it is transitive in the same way as *al-'ilm* (knowledge) is transitive.

﴿that they will never be resurrected﴾. *An* together with what follows it stands in the place of the two objects, and its estimated form is "*annahum lan yub'athu*" (that they will never be resurrected).

﴿Say: Yes﴾. This is an affirmation of what follows *lan*, which is the resurrection.

﴿By my Lord, you will surely be resurrected﴾. He emphasized the report with an oath. If you ask: what is the meaning of swearing an oath about something they deny? I say: it is permissible, because a threat made with it has a greater impact on the heart. It is as if it were said to them: "What you deny is certainly going to happen."

﴿Then you will surely be informed of what you did﴾, i.e., the resurrection.

﴿That is easy for God﴾, meaning easy, not difficult.

So believe in Allah and His Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ),

and the Light which We have sent down, meaning the Qur'an, because it makes clear the reality of everything, so that one is guided by it, just as one is guided by light,

and Allah is Acquainted with what you do. So be mindful of your affairs.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verse 9:

﴿The day He gathers you together﴾: the adverbial phrase (zarf) is in the accusative, governed either by His words "you will surely be informed" (latunabba'unna), or by an implied "remember" (udhkur).

﴿For the Day of Gathering﴾: on that day the first and the last will be gathered together.

﴿That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain﴾: this is used figuratively from "the people lost out (taghabana) in trade", which means that some of them defraud one another, because the happy are brought down to the stations of the wretched, which they would have occupied had they been wretched, and the wretched are raised to the stations of the happy, which they would have occupied had they been happy, as has been related in the hadith. The meaning of "That is the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain" – although people may defraud one another on other days – is to magnify that day, and that its mutual loss and gain is true loss and gain, not the loss and gain of worldly affairs.

﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds﴾: this is an adjective of the verbal noun, meaning "a righteous deed".

﴿He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him﴾: with the nun (nun) in both verbs, as read by the people of Medina and Syria.

﴿into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

(p-٤٩٣) ﴿No calamity strikes except by the permission of Allah﴾: [calamity means] hardship, sickness, the death of a family member, or anything that causes distress.

﴿Except by the permission of Allah﴾: by His knowledge, His decree, and His will, as if He had permitted the calamity to befall him.

﴿And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart﴾: to make istirja' (the saying "Indeed we belong to Allah, and to Him we will return") at the time of calamity, until he says it. Or: He expands his heart to increase in obedience and goodness. Or: "He guides his heart until he knows that what befell him was never going to miss him, and what missed him was never going to befall him." And from Mujahid: "If he is tested, he is patient; if he is given something, he is grateful; if he is wronged, he forgives."

﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verse 12:

﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away﴾, from the obedience of Allah and the obedience of His Messenger,

﴿then upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾, that is: upon him is only the conveying (of the message), and he has indeed done so.

"Allah— there is no god but He. So let the believers put their trust in Allah." (Qur'an 64:13)

This is an incitement (ba'th) for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to rely upon Him (al-tawakkul), so that He may give him victory over those who denied him and turned away from him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verse 15:

﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾, a test and a tribulation, because they lead one into sin and punishment, and there is no trial greater than these two.

﴿And with Allah is a great reward﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter, and that is greater than the benefit you gain from your wealth and your children. He did not introduce "min" (from) into it, as in the case of enmity (in verse 14), because all of them are not free from being a trial and from preoccupying the heart, whereas some of them may be free from enmity.

﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾: that is, with your utmost effort and capacity. It has been said that this explains His words "as He deserves to be feared."

﴿And listen﴾: to what you are admonished with.

﴿And obey﴾: in what you are commanded and forbidden.

﴿And spend﴾: in the causes for which spending has become obligatory upon you.

﴿Good for yourselves﴾: that is, spend in a manner that is good for yourselves. Al-Kisa'i (al-Kisa'i) said: "Let the spending be good for your souls." The most correct view is that its implied meaning is: "Bring forth what is better for yourselves than wealth and children, and what you are devoted to of love of desires and the adornments of this world."

﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul﴾: that is, from miserliness (al-bukhl) in giving the obligatory zakat (zakat, obligatory almsgiving) and sadaqa (sadaqa, voluntary or obligatory charity).

﴿Those are the successful.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 64, verses 17–18:

﴿If you lend to Allah a good loan﴾: with good intention and sincerity. The mention of "loan" is a gentle way of inviting (giving).

﴿He will multiply it for you﴾: He will record for you ten times the one, or seven hundred, up to whatever amount He wills of increase.

﴿And forgive you. And Allah is Appreciative [Shakur]﴾: He accepts the little and gives the abundant.

﴿Forbearing [Halim]﴾: He pardons the great one's sin for the miser, or He multiplies the charity for the one who gives it, and does not hasten punishment for the one who withholds it.

﴿Knower of the unseen﴾, that is, He knows what is hidden within the secrets of hearts.

﴿And the witnessed﴾, (p-495) that is, what is manifest of outward calamities.

﴿The Almighty [al-Aziz]﴾, the One who grants might by manifesting the defects [of the concealed].

﴿The Wise [al-Hakim]﴾, in informing about the unseen matters.
